description:
Somos un equipo de estudiantes universitarios y apasionados por los datos.

Nos dedicamos a explorar, analizar y mejorar la manera en que los datos se presentan e interpretan, buscando fuentes de información más confiables y nuevas perspectivas que impulsen la investigación y el conocimiento.

We are dedicated to analyzing, and improving the way data is presented. Our goal is to identify more reliable sources of information and discover new perspectives that drive research and expand knowledge.
summary:
Goal: Make relevant Earth observation data easier to find, obtain and understand for the Moquegua region of Peru. The project aims to help people access reliable, quality-screened information for a specific region without having to navigate large global datasets themselves.

The long-term vision is to support students, researchers, farmers and other regional users working on rainfall, land-surface temperature, agriculture, farming and disaster prevention. Easier access to regional observations could also support future weather-forecasting projects. This pilot presents historical observations; it does not generate forecasts or operational disaster warnings.
details:
Goal

Make relevant Earth observation data easier to find, obtain and understand for the Moquegua region of Peru. The project aims to help people access reliable, quality-screened information for a specific region without having to navigate large global datasets themselves.

The long-term vision is to support students, researchers, farmers and other regional users working on rainfall, land-surface temperature, agriculture, farming and disaster prevention. Easier access to regional observations could also support future weather-forecasting projects. This pilot presents historical observations; it does not generate forecasts or operational disaster warnings.

Tasks done

  • Investigated NASA Earthdata availability and access for the full Moquegua department.
  • Retrieved rainfall observations and established a processing pipeline from source data to a regional visualization cache.
  • Used a department boundary polygon to intersect and clip the data to Moquegua, rather than treating every overlapping rectangular footprint as relevant regional coverage.
  • Applied data-quality filtering and an 80% usable-area threshold to assess whether enough of the region has usable observations. Missing or rejected observations remain distinct from genuine zero rainfall.
  • Built a simple visualization page with a regional map, rainfall values, a date selector, coverage information and a lightweight map fallback.

The boundary used in this pilot was obtained from Osinergmin's public departmental map service. Its lineage to INEI has not been verified, so it is not described here as verified INEI data. The outline remains provisional; its source release, reuse terms and legal authority require clarification.
